subject: proposed foothill overlay
comment: Please forward this to planning commission. Planning Commissioners: I watched the town hall meeting and I noticed a few issues that were concerning. Because the citizens were not able to have a conversation about this in person, face to face, it made it hard to get their questions answered to their satisfaction. When a question was asked by email and it wasn’t answered correctly the conversation stopped because they weren’t able to say “No, that’s not what I meant,” and have the conversation continue. It’s also very confusing to have to make a phone call and get your questions answered without being able to point to maps etc. For this reason (and others) to vote on an issue that is so controversial, I feel should be continued until face to face in person conversations can be held. Too many questions are unanswered. Another issue I saw was I don’t think all the flaws have been ironed out. For example. Brandon Larsen said that there still needs to be a study done on ridgelines and Bill Peperone said “they have not had a chance to get to it” when another issue was brought up. To me this shows that they need more time to make this right. There was conversation about the subcommittee that was formed to plan this overlay. Mr. Handley said that the overlay plan was “not initiated by anyone outside the city council and the subcommittee members” but I know for a fact that there was a citizens group formed that was against a development. (This group was contacted and asked why large landowners were not included in this group and their response was they would be contacted and included but they never were. This group only wanted those included that felt the same way they did.) This group put a tremendous amount of pressure on the city and council to do something so development wouldn’t happen because they wanted to look and hike on private property. So I feel there was a lot of outside influence from a one-sided group. When this issue was before the planning commission the first time there weren’t many comments because the citizens didn’t know about it. It also seemed like, because of some comments made by the commissioners, that they really weren’t voting how they felt because there seemed to be so much pressure to ram this proposal through. I hope this won’t be the case now. I hope all commissioners take their time to study this to make sure it is done correctly. The map has been revised and that is a great improvement. But won’t it cause a lot of confusion with the little pockets of property here and there that are still included? These pockets are mostly in already established neighborhoods and can be controlled by existing rules if ever developed. Thank you Janie Gillespie Sent from Mail for Windows 10
